# Seated Liberty Dollar

The Seated Liberty dollar was struck from 1840 to 1873, the last
silver dollar series before the Coinage Act of 1873 suspended the
denomination and triggered the "Crime of '73" controversy.

Christian Gobrecht's design shows Liberty seated on a rock, holding a
liberty pole and a shield. The same seated motif appeared across the
half dime through half dollar denominations for most of the
nineteenth century.

Circulation strikes are scarce in high grade because most pieces went
west or were exported to Asia in trade; the 1870-S is a famous rarity
with perhaps a dozen known.

Related: [[Coin Silver Standards]], [[Morgan Dollar]].
